_comment: DECLARED inbound network posture, per host. The SoT the reconciler's POSTURE_DRIFT check asserts against. Retires the generator 'inbound exposure is an emergent property of whatever each service happened to bind'. Every other layer in this system has a SoT plus a canary; before OPS-HOST-EXPOSURE-POSTURE-W1 the network did not, which is why 'ufw is inactive' sat in an audit report instead of firing an alert. Changing a rule here does NOT change enforcement — enforcement is the Hetzner Cloud Firewall, mutated only by a human-dispatched wave. This file is what makes a drift DETECTABLE, not what applies it.
_host_label_semantics: `host` keys are OPAQUE STABLE LABELS (`signal-1`, `aoe-1`), never addresses — same contract as monitoring-inventory.json. Label -> address resolution happens in ~/.ssh/config or the host's own MONITORING_* env, NEVER from this committed JSON: this repo is PUBLIC. Unlike the inventory, this file has NO legacy rows, so it carries zero literal addresses and must stay that way.
_allowed_sources_semantics: Named source ALIASES resolved at apply/probe time (see `source_aliases`), never literal CIDRs. A literal here would be a published address AND a value that silently rots when the upstream range changes. `any` is permitted but must carry a `justification` — an unexplained `any` reads as an oversight to the next reader; a justified one reads as a decision.
_expected_from_peer_derivation: SINGLE-DERIVATION RULE — do NOT add a second field for this. A port's expected reachability from the PEER host is derived from `allowed_sources` alone: reachable IFF (`any` is present) OR (the probing peer's own host label is present). Everything else is expected CLOSED from the peer vantage. Consequence worth stating because it is the obvious false-fire: a port restricted to `cloudflare` is correctly UNREACHABLE from the peer host, and POSTURE_DRIFT must not read that as an outage.

_classification_semantics.must-stay-public: genuinely needs `any`; no narrowing possible without breaking a confirmed dependency
_classification_semantics.restrict-to-source: reachable, but only from an enumerable source set
_classification_semantics.asserted-any: open to the world as a RATIFIED DECISION, not an oversight; requires `justification` naming the wave that would narrow it
_classification_semantics.already-loopback: bound to 127.0.0.1 — needs no firewall rule at all; recorded so a future rebind to 0.0.0.0 is caught by POSTURE_DRIFT on its first cycle
_classification_semantics.declared-closed: deliberately unreachable from the internet; access is via another path (SSH tunnel, Cloudflare Tunnel)

_enforcement_semantics: The Hetzner Cloud Firewall is the ONLY enforcement layer, deliberately. It is enforced OUTSIDE the VM, so a bad rule cannot sever console access the way a bad `ufw enable` can, and it is not bypassed by Docker's iptables chains. See `in_vm_layer` per host for why nothing runs inside the VM. NO AUTOMATED MUTATION: an unattended job must never change a network rule — POSTURE_DRIFT detects and alerts, a human-dispatched wave applies. That limit is deliberate, not a gap.

any.note: the absence of a restriction, stated explicitly

cloudflare.note: 15 IPv4 + 7 IPv6 as measured 2026-07-30 — comfortably inside Hetzner's 500-effective-rules/firewall cap. Re-resolved at apply time; never pinned as literals here. Contrast `github-actions` below.

github-actions.note: NOT USABLE AS AN ALLOWLIST — recorded so the next reader does not re-derive the same dead end. 7,297 CIDRs (5,658 IPv4 / 1,639 IPv6, ~27.9M IPv4 addresses) measured 2026-07-30, against a Hetzner ceiling of 500 effective rules x 5 firewalls = 2,500 per server. Not 'large and churning' — not expressible. This is why signal-1:22 is `asserted-any` rather than allowlisted.

operator.note: DYNAMIC (residential). Deliberately never pinned as a literal rule: a pinned dynamic /32 either drifts into a silent deny or becomes a rule POSTURE_DRIFT flags forever. Where operator access to a restricted port is needed, the path is an SSH tunnel over port 22, not a firewall entry.

signal-1.role: public — algovault.com, api.algovault.com, plausible.algovault.com, Caddy, MCP server, Postgres, Redis, Plausible

ufw.evidence: Established empirically on this box, not asserted from general knowledge: published container ports are DNAT'd in `nat/PREROUTING -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL -j DOCKER` and then traverse `filter/FORWARD`, never `filter/INPUT` where ufw's user rules live. `iptables -S | grep -c ufw` = 0. Host processes (sshd, caddy) DO traverse INPUT. Net effect: ufw would govern ONLY 22/80/443 — the ports we intend to leave open — and would govern NONE of the container ports that constitute actual exposure. That is lockout risk and false assurance in exchange for zero enforcement.
ufw.do_not_re_litigate: This is a RECORDED EMPIRICAL NEGATIVE. A future wave proposing to 'add ufw for defense in depth' would reintroduce the lockout risk believing it helps. If an in-VM layer is ever genuinely wanted, the lever is DOCKER-USER (below), not ufw.

docker_user_chain.rationale: DOCKER-USER exists on this host and is INTENTIONALLY empty. It is the one chain consulted BEFORE Docker's own ACCEPT rules, so it is the correct in-VM lever if one is ever needed — but it is redundant underneath an out-of-VM cloud firewall. Declared here so its emptiness is not mistaken for unfinished work.

inbound.purpose: SSH. Three confirmed consumers: (1) GitHub Actions auto-deploy (appleboy/ssh-action, .github/workflows/deploy.yml), (2) the aoe-1 -> signal-1 Postgres tunnel, which dials OUT from aoe-1 and therefore needs inbound 22 here, (3) operator administration and the recovery path.
inbound.justification: Ratified A2. An allowlist is mechanically impossible at the enforcement layer — see source_aliases.github-actions. Narrowing this to operator + aoe-1 requires moving deploy off inbound SSH entirely, which is OPS-DEPLOY-PULL-MODEL-W{NEXT}. Deliberately NOT bundled into a firewall wave: a broken deploy would leave us unable to deploy the fix.
inbound.hardening: Compensating controls, since the port stays open: key-only auth enforced server-side (PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no) and fail2ban proven to actually ban. Both are asserted by this wave, not assumed.

inbound.purpose: HTTP->HTTPS redirect (308 on every path, verified) and the ACME HTTP-01 challenge path.
inbound.justification: DEFERRED, not overlooked — the CF-only narrowing hit a ratified HALT branch. The ruling was 'DNS-01 first, then restrict', precisely so renewal stops depending on any inbound path. DNS-01 turned out to be blocked by an unstated prerequisite: this host runs Caddy 2.6.2, which ships NO dns.providers module and has NO `add-package` subcommand (that arrived in 2.7). DNS-01 therefore requires replacing the Caddy binary on the host serving all public traffic — a materially larger change than configuration, five days before the Aug 4-5 renewal. Forcing it is exactly what the HALT branch exists to prevent.

inbound.purpose: All public traffic: landing, /verify, api.algovault.com, /api/merkle-batches, Stripe webhooks, x402 + Circle Gateway settlement callbacks.
inbound.justification: DEFERRED with the same HALT branch as :80 — see that entry. Recording the finding so the follow-up wave does not re-derive it: ~300 requests/24h reach this origin DIRECTLY, bypassing Cloudflare, proven by raw-IP Host headers (232x '<origin>:80', 68x bare origin IP) which cannot have transited CF because CF always forwards the original hostname; 68 probed /.well-known/acme-challenge/, a cert-takeover recon pattern. The origin answers https with a valid publicly-trusted certificate, so CF's WAF, rate-limiting and bot-management are OPTIONAL for anyone who knows the address — and the address is irreversibly published. This is the highest-value narrowing still outstanding.
inbound.narrowing_prework_already_done: Gate 1 of the ratified order is COMPLETE and need not be repeated: all 11 A/AAAA/CNAME records on the zone were enumerated, and all three that resolve to this origin (algovault.com, api.algovault.com, plausible.algovault.com) are PROXIED. The single DNS-only record, blog.algovault.com, CNAMEs to hashnode.network and resolves into Hashnode's own hosting — it never touches this origin, so a CF-only rule blackholes nothing. Cloudflare publishes 22 source CIDRs, comfortably inside the 500-rule cap.
inbound.open_question_for_the_follow_up: Whether DNS-01 is needed at all, or whether a CF-only rule is safe under the EXISTING HTTP-01 path. The deduction that it is safe: every hostname is CF-proxied, so Let's Encrypt cannot reach this origin directly and renewal must already transit Cloudflare today; TLS-ALPN-01 cannot traverse a CF proxy because CF terminates TLS, so HTTP-01-via-CF is necessarily the working path, and restricting to CF ranges would not change it. That is a DEDUCTION, not a measurement, and the ratified rule is 'prove issuance end-to-end, never switch-and-assume'. Proving it means forcing a real obtain, which is itself the thing the HALT branch forbids doing days before renewal. After the Aug 4-5 renewal completes there is a clean ~3-month runway in which to force one safely.

inbound.purpose: HTTP/3 (QUIC). Caddy binds *:443/udp; must track the TCP rule or H3 clients silently fall back.
inbound.justification: Tracks the :443/tcp ruling exactly — deferred under the same HALT branch. Narrowing these two apart would leave H3 clients failing over to TCP for reasons no one would connect back to a firewall change.

inbound.purpose: ICMP. Deliberately allowed rather than swept up in the default-deny.
inbound.justification: Availability, not convenience: blocking inbound ICMP breaks Path MTU Discovery (the `fragmentation-needed` reply), which manifests as large HTTPS responses hanging on any path with a reduced MTU — a failure mode that looks nothing like a firewall rule and would be debugged for hours. Hetzner's firewall is stateful, but its docs do not state whether related ICMP errors are exempted, so this is allowed EXPLICITLY rather than assumed. Negligible attack surface; a real availability risk if omitted.
inbound.narrowed_by_wave: none — ICMP is not a narrowing candidate; this entry exists to record the decision, not to defer it

loopback_only.note: the DB holding internal-only outcome_return_pct / outcome-WR data — this bind is the control SECURITY-AUDIT-FULL-W1 flagged as load-bearing-and-alone

aoe-1.role: AOE — Prefect, shadow evaluator, promotion scanner, AOE workers, agent-facing MCP

ufw.evidence: Same empirical chain as signal-1, verified independently on this box: `iptables -S | grep -c ufw` = 0, and the DNAT-to-FORWARD path bypasses filter/INPUT. This host makes the point sharpest — its ONE world-exposed container port (8080) carries a nat/DOCKER rule with NO `-d 127.0.0.1/32` constraint, unlike every loopback-published port here, and a `ufw deny 8080` would not have touched it.

docker_user_chain.rationale: See signal-1. Empty by intent, not by omission.

inbound.purpose: SSH. Consumers: operator administration + rsync-based AOE deploy (this host has no git checkout and no CI auto-deploy), and the recovery path.
inbound.justification: Ratified A2. Unlike signal-1 there is no GitHub Actions constraint here, so this port COULD narrow to the operator — but the operator address is dynamic (see source_aliases.operator) and port 22 is the recovery path with no in-band fallback. Pinning a drifting /32 to the one port you would need during a lockout trades a real availability risk for a marginal reduction. Revisit if a stable operator vantage (bastion or Cloudflare Tunnel) ever exists.
inbound.hardening: Key-only auth already enforced server-side on this host (PasswordAuthentication no, verified via `sshd -T`); fail2ban asserted by this wave.

inbound.evidence: 14,654 retained access lines: 14,434x 404, 220x 401, and exactly ONE 200 — a ListToolsRequest from the operator's own address. ZERO hits from signal-1. The path fingerprint is textbook mass-scanning: /login, /.env, /.env.production, /.git/config, /goform/set_LimitClient_cfg. A published port whose only successful caller is the operator testing it is not a product surface, it is a leftover.
inbound.why_no_operator_entry: Refines the ratified D2 'operator + signal-1' two-entry list to zero entries, because the evidence removed both: signal-1 has never called it, and the operator address is dynamic. Operator access is preserved via an SSH tunnel over port 22 (`ssh -L 8080:127.0.0.1:8080 aoe-1`), which is strictly better than pinning a rotting /32. One-line revert if the architect disagrees: add `operator` to allowed_sources.
inbound.additional_risk_closed: The listener is PLAINTEXT HTTP — a TLS handshake to :8080 fails. Bearer tokens were crossing the public internet in cleartext to a box holding AOE model artifacts.
inbound.end_state_wave: OPS-AOE-MCP-BEHIND-TUNNEL-W{NEXT} — rebind to loopback behind Cloudflare Tunnel + Zero Trust Access. This is configuration, not new infrastructure: cloudflared already runs on this host serving aoe.algovault.com -> 127.0.0.1:4200 (tunnel 6454e5f8-...), so exposing the MCP is an extra ingress stanza plus a DNS record. Preferring a loopback rebind over a firewall rule is the standing rule; the firewall is the reversible interim while an agent-facing endpoint's URL and auth model change under their own wave.

inbound.purpose: ICMP. Same ruling as signal-1 — see that entry's justification.
inbound.justification: Availability, not convenience: blocking inbound ICMP breaks Path MTU Discovery, a failure mode that looks nothing like a firewall rule. Allowed explicitly rather than assumed, because Hetzner's docs do not state whether its stateful firewall exempts related ICMP errors. Kept identical across both hosts so the two postures do not diverge for no reason.
inbound.narrowed_by_wave: none — ICMP is not a narrowing candidate; this entry records the decision rather than deferring it

loopback_only.note: reachable externally ONLY via Cloudflare Tunnel + Zero Trust Access at aoe.algovault.com — the pattern 8080 should adopt

loopback_only.owner: aoe-pg-tunnel.service (ssh -N -L; also binds docker bridge gateways 172.17.0.1/172.18.0.1 so containers can reach it)

aoe-1.outbound_note: cloudflared holds several high-numbered *:udp sockets (QUIC). These are OUTBOUND sockets, not inbound services, and must not be declared as inbound ports or POSTURE_DRIFT will chase ephemeral port numbers every cycle.
